chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Amr ibn Abi Nasr said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the Maghrib prayer: 'When the disk [of the sun] disappears, it is the time for the prayer, and break your fast.'

key_terms.تَوَارَى الْقُرْصُ: The disappearance of the disk (referring to the sun setting completely)

ai.seo_question: When does the time for Maghrib prayer begin according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Amr ibn Abi Nasr, clarifies the precise astronomical marker for Maghrib as the complete disappearance of the solar disk (ghurub), distinguishing it from the onset of twilight (shuruq). In Shia fiqh, this definition is critical for determining the validity of fasting and the timing of the Maghrib prayer, ensuring adherence to the divine command without premature or delayed observance. The emphasis on 'if the disk has vanished' underscores the necessity of visual confirmation or established astronomical calculation in determining the exact moment of sunset.
